questions.question: While driving, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to tell others what you plan to do.
Use turn signals only if another vehicle is next to you.
Do not use a turn signal if your lane change is obvious.
Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: You must always use turn signals. This tells other drivers what you are doing.

questions.question: Loose belts in an engine compartment will:

options.text: Prevent the water pump and fan from working properly. This causes the engine to overheat.
Make the engine run better.
Make the fan work too much. This makes the engine run too cold.
Last longer than tight belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the water pump and fan from working properly. This causes the engine to overheat.
questions.explanation: Check your engine belts to make sure they are tight. Loose belts will not work right. This can cause your engine to overheat.

questions.question: After you change a tire, you should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the tire tread is good.
Make sure you changed the right tire.
Check if rocks are in the tire tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you change a tire, stop after a short distance and check that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: Buses must never transport:

options.text: Small arms ammunition.
Soft drinks.
Open food.
Tear gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tear gas.
questions.explanation: Buses may carry some hazardous materials. However, they can never carry tear gas or similar irritating materials.

questions.question: After you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Stay on.
Flash on and off.
Turn off right away.
Turn off once you start moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off right away.
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, all warning lights and buzzers should turn off immediately. This includes the charging light, oil light, coolant light, and ABS light.

questions.question: Before you drive a bus, you must:

options.text: Read the most recent inspection report.
Wash the outside.
Clean the inside.
Count the seats.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the most recent inspection report.
questions.explanation: Before you drive a bus, you must check the most recent inspection report. Only drive the bus if any problems have been fixed or have been approved as not needing to be fixed.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, your four-way flashers should:

options.text: Turn on before you cross railroad tracks.
Never be used.
Only be used after you cross railroad tracks.
Only be used near railroad tracks if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on before you cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: When driving a school bus, turn on your four-way flashers as you approach and cross railroad tracks. Turn them off once your whole vehicle has passed the tracks.

questions.question: Federal and state laws require:

options.text: Drivers to check their vehicles on a regular basis.
Drivers to check their vehicles only if they think there may be a problem.
Drivers to check their vehicles only before traveling out-of-state.
Drivers to check their vehicles only if they will carry hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers to check their vehicles on a regular basis.
questions.explanation: Commercial drivers must check their vehicles before every trip. Regular checks help you find problems before they become dangerous and costly.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Only comes from physical distraction, not mental distraction.
Gets worse if you pre-program radio stations.
Can be avoided by eating while you drive.
Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while you drive.
questions.explanation: Do not have complex or emotional conversations while driving. Pre-program your radio before you start driving. Do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Mental distractions are just as dangerous as physical distractions.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Stop on the tracks.
Change gears.
Try to pass another vehicle.
Stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks, do not stop on the tracks. Do not change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: Before driving a bus that has been parked for a few days, what should you do?

options.text: Assume the interior is working correctly.
Call the local police department.
Walk through the bus to check for any damage since the last trip.
Ask passengers to check the interior of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for any damage since the last trip.
questions.explanation: People sometimes damage buses that are parked unattended. Before driving, check the interior to make sure everything is in good condition.

questions.question: Why should you be careful around a stopped bus?

options.text: It is not a concern.
It is not a concern if passengers are not getting off.
It should not be on the road.
It is a concern whether you can see passengers or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a concern whether you can see passengers or not.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front of or behind the bus. The bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: When checking a power steering system, what should you look for?

options.text: The fluid is at the correct level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.
The hoses are empty.
Only small leaks are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the correct level.
questions.explanation: Check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level in the power steering system. Look for leaks and fix them before driving.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?

options.text: One-sixteenth of a second
One-eighth of a second
Between three-quarters and one second
Two seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Between three-quarters and one second
questions.explanation: The average driver takes between three-quarters and one second to react to something.

questions.question: What should a driver do before driving a bus that has been parked for a few days?

options.text: Assume the interior is in good condition.
Call the local police to inspect the bus.
Walk through the bus to check that no damage has occurred since the last trip.
Ask passengers to check the interior of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check that no damage has occurred since the last trip.
questions.explanation: Parked buses can get damaged by others. Before each trip, check the interior to make sure all systems are working safely for passengers.

questions.question: What is the best way to back up a bus?

options.text: Use only the passenger-side mirror.
Back up quickly.
Turn toward the passenger side when possible.
Use a helper if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper if possible.
questions.explanation: Back up slowly and use both side mirrors. Have someone help watch your blind spots when you can. Agree on a signal to stop.

questions.question: After stopping during the stop/start test, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the parking brake.
Keep the vehicle in first gear.
Be perpendicular to the curb.
Block a driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake.
questions.explanation: When parking during the stop/start test, apply the parking brake. Shift into neutral or park. Park parallel to the curb and do not block driveways or intersections.

questions.question: When should placards be used on a vehicle?

options.text: Any time the vehicle carries hazardous materials.
If there is empty space in the truck.
If hazardous materials exceed 200 pounds.
If the materials create an inhalation hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time the vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show what type of materials are being carried and warn others of any hazards.

questions.question: What must never be carried in the passenger area of a bus?

options.text: Small arms ammunition
An oxygen tank
Radioactive materials
Passengers who are drunk

questions.correctAnswerText: Radioactive materials
questions.explanation: Buses must never carry labeled radioactive materials in areas where passengers sit.

questions.question: How do you know if a bus is going too fast around a banked curve?

options.text: The bus leans toward the outside of the curve.
The bus leans toward the inside of the curve.
The bus feels unnatural.
An alarm sounds on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bus leans toward the outside of the curve.
questions.explanation: If a bus leans toward the outside of a banked curve, it is going too fast. Slow down before curves, especially in large vehicles like buses.
